Nirjala Ekadashi- The Sacred Waterless Fast
purpose.addtional_description:
Nirjala Ekadashi, observed on the 11th day of Shukla Paksha in the Hindu month of Jyeshtha (June 25, 2026), is the most powerful and spiritually significant of all Ekadashi fasts.

The term "Nirjala" means "without water," making this the strictest fasting observance where devotees abstain completely from both food and water for the entire day. This sacred day grants the combined spiritual merit of all 24 Ekadashis observed throughout the year and is dedicated to Lord Vishnu, also known as Bhimseni Ekadashi due to its association with Bhima's devotion.

steps: Holy Bath and Sankalp Take a ritual bath before sunrise and formally vow to observe the waterless fast for Lord Vishnu's blessings.
Morning Puja Worship Lord Vishnu with Tulsi leaves, flowers, sandalwood, and ghee lamps at the home temple.
Continuous Chanting Recite "Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya" mantra and Vishnu Sahasranama throughout the day.
Charity and Service Donate water pots, food, clothes to Brahmins and needy people while setting up water stalls for public service.
Parana (Breaking Fast) Break the complete waterless fast on Dwadashi morning by drinking water first, then Tulsi leaves, followed by sattvic food.

Among followers of Hinduism, Jamai Shashti is regarded as both a social and spiritual festival. On this occasion, Goddess Shashti is also worshipped with devotion.

purpose.addtional_description:
It is observed on the new moon day (Amavasya) of the Bhadrapada month, marking the end of Pitru Paksha (the fortnight dedicated to ancestors) and the beginning of Devi Paksha (the fortnight dedicated to Goddess Durga). 

Mahalaya Amavasya represents a sacred day of prayer, remembrance, and preparation for welcoming Goddess Durga to Earth. On this day, people perform Tarpan and Shraddha rituals to pay homage to their ancestors, seeking blessings for peace, prosperity, and protection. 

**Why Mahalaya is Important-**
**End of Pitru Paksha:** The two-week period before Mahalaya is dedicated to offering food, prayers, and water (Tarpan) to ancestors. Mahalaya marks its completion. 
**Beginning of Devi Paksha:** From this day onwards, the energy shifts towards devotion to Goddess Durga, setting the stage for Durga Puja celebrations.

steps: Shraddha: Ritual food offerings made to forefathers at Gaya or home
Tarpan: Offering water, sesame seeds, and prayers to ancestors on riverbanks or at home.
Listening to Mahishasura Mardini: A radio recital by Birendra Krishna Bhadra has become a cultural tradition in Bengal.
Early Morning Prayers: Devotees wake up before sunrise to perform spiritual practices.

purpose.description: Navratri is a nine days festival dedicated to Goddess Durga
purpose.addtional_description:
Navratri is a Sanskrit word which literally means nine nights. During these nine nights and ten days, Goddess Durga is worshipped in 9 different forms, known as Navdurga. The tenth day is celebrated as Vijayadashami when idols of Goddess Durga are immersed into the water body.

Navratri is very popular festival in the western states of Gujarat, Maharashtra and the southern state of Karnataka.

In West Bengal Navratri is celebrated as Durga Puja. In West Bengal, Goddess Durga is worshipped on the last three days of Navratri and these three days are famously known as Durga Saptami, Durga Ashtami and Durga Navami

purpose.description: Ghatasthapana marks the beginning of nine days festivity
purpose.addtional_description: After the self-immolation as Goddess Sati, Goddess Parvati took birth as the daughter of Lord Himalaya. In Sanskrit Shail means the mountain and due to which Goddess was known as Shailputri, the daughter of the mountain. Goddess Shailputri is worshipped on the first day of Navratri

purpose.description: Brahmacharini Puja is performed on the second day of Navratri
purpose.addtional_description:
After Kushmanda form, Goddess Parvati took birth at the home of Daksha Prajapati. In this form the Goddess Parvati was a great Sati and her unmarried form is worshipped as Goddess Brahmacharini.

Goddess Brahmacharini is worshipped on the second day of Navratri. She is the goddess of penance and devotion. The name Brahmacharini means one who practices penance and austerity. She is depicted as a fair-complexioned goddess, holding a rosary in her right hand and a water utensil in her left hand.

purpose.description: Chandraghanta Puja is performed on the third day of Navratri
purpose.addtional_description: Goddess Chandraghanta is the married form the Goddess Parvati. After getting married to Lord Shiva Goddess Mahagauri started adorning her forehead with half Chandra and due to which Goddess Parvati was known as Goddess Chandraghanta.

purpose.description: Kushmanda Puja is performed on the fourth day of Navratri
purpose.addtional_description: After taking form of Siddhidatri, Goddess Parvati started living inside the center of the Sun so that He can liberate energy to the universe. Since then Goddess is known as Kushmanda. Kushmanda is the Goddess who has the power and capability to live inside the Sun. The glow and radiance of her body is as luminous as that of the Sun.

purpose.description: Skandamata Puja is performed on the fifth day of Navratri
purpose.addtional_description: Skandamata means 'Mother of Skanda' in Sanskrit. Skanda is another name for Kartikeya, the war god who became the commander of lord Shiva's divine army.

purpose.description: Katyayani Puja is performed on the sixth day of Navratri
purpose.addtional_description: Katyayani is the sixth form of Goddess Durga. She is worshipped on the sixth day of Navratri. To destroy demon Mahishasura, Goddess Parvati took the form of Goddess Katyayani. It was the most violent form of Goddess Parvati. In this form Goddess Parvati is also known as Warrior Goddess. She is depicted as a fierce goddess riding a lion and carrying weapons in her hands.

purpose.description: The first day of Saraswati Puja during Navratri is known as Saraswati Avahan.
Goddess Kalaratri is worshipped on the seventh day of Navratri.
purpose.addtional_description: When the Goddess Parvati removed outer golden skin to kill demons named Shumbha and Nishumbha, She was known as Goddess Kalaratri. Kalaratri is the fiercest and the most ferocious form of Goddess Parvati.

purpose.description: Saraswati Puja is performed on the eighth day of Navratri
purpose.addtional_description: The second day of Saraswati Puja during Navratri is known as Saraswati Pradhan Puja day. Pradhan Puja day is the main Saraswati Puja day.

purpose.description: Kalparambha and Akal Bodhon- ceremonial beginning of Durga Puja
purpose.addtional_description:
Kalparambha is the ceremonial beginning of Durga Puja rituals, performed on the sixth day (Shashti Tithi) of the festival. It involves installing a sacred pot (Kalash) filled with water and invoking Goddess Durga to reside either in a Bilva tree or the Kalash. This ritual, also known as Bilva Nimantran in other parts of India, sets the stage for the main festivities and is equivalent to Ghatasthapana performed during Navratri in other regions. 

Akal Bodhon means 'untimely awakening' of Goddess Durga. According to legend, when Lord Rama needed to fight Ravana, he was advised by Brahma to awaken Goddess Durga during her sleep period (the six months when gods remain asleep, during the sun's southward journey). This awakening of the sleeping goddess during an 'untimely' period established the tradition of Durga Puja during Sharad Navratri

steps: Ghatasthapana (Kalash Installation)- Install a sacred earthen pot (ghata) filled with Ganga water, mango leaves, and twigs of various trees including Asvattha (fig), Bata (Indian fig), Asoka, and jackfruit
Kalash Decoration- Decorate the Kalash with turmeric, vermilion, and flowers
Sankalp (Resolution): The family head takes a sacred vow to perform Durga Puja rituals authentically for the next three days (Maha Saptami, Maha Ashtami, and Maha Navami)
Bilva Tree Worship: Invoke Goddess Durga to reside in a Bilva (Bael) tree or the Kalash
Goddess Invitation (Amantran): Sacred act of inviting the goddess to accept the puja

purpose.description: Maha Saptami is also known as Navpatrika Puja(Kolabou Puja) and it is the first day of Durga Puja
purpose.addtional_description:
On Maha Saptami day Goddess Durga is invoked in a group of nine plants known as Navpatrika. Navpatrika is formed by bundling nine different plants including the branch of Bilva tree of the previous day. After that Navpatrika is given a ceremonial bath, adorned with a red or orange colored cloth and installed on a wooden seat on the right side of image of Durga.

Maha Saptami Puja begins with Mahasnan. For Maha Snan a mirror is placed on a platter in such a way that the reflection of the Goddess Durga is seen in the mirror. It is the refection of Goddess Durga in the mirror which is given the ritualistic bath using various materials. After bath ceremony the ritual of Prana Pratishtha (प्राण प्रतिष्ठा) takes place

steps: Kolabou Snan: Sacred bath of nine plants in river/water body before sunrise
Mahasnan: Mirror ritual where Goddess Durga's reflection is bathed with puja essentials
Navpatrika Installation: Nine plants (banana, kacchi, turmeric, bilva, barley, pomegranate, asoka, manaka, rice) tied together and installed
Shodashopachara Puja: Sixteen-step elaborate worship with traditional offerings
Prana Pratishtha: Divine energy invocation into Goddess idol and Navpatrika

purpose.description: Mahashtami, also known as Maha Durgashtami, is second day of Durga Puja
purpose.addtional_description:
Maha Ashtami is one of the most important days of Durga Puja. On Maha Ashtami nine small pots are installed and nine Shaktis of Durga are invoked in them. All nine forms of Goddess Durga are worshipped during Maha Ashtami Puja. Young unmarried girls, being treated as Goddess Durga itself, are also worshipped on Maha Ashtami. Worshipping of young girls during Durga Puja is known as Kumari Puja

Sandhi Puja is also falls on Maha Ashtami. The time window of the last 24 minutes of Ashtami Tithi and the first 24 minutes of Navami Tithi is known as Sandhi Time or the holy juncture during Durga Puja. Sandhi time is considered the most auspicious time during whole Durga Puja.

steps: Mahasnan: Ritual bath before sunrise for devotees
Kumari Puja: Worship nine young girls (ages 2-10) as living forms of Goddess Durga
Sandhi Puja: 48-minute ritual at Ashtami-Navami junction - most intense moment with 108 lamps and specific mantras
Pushpanjali: Three rounds of flower offerings with mantras (morning, midday, before Sandhi Puja)

steps: Sandhi Puja (48-minute Ceremony): Performed at the exact junction of Ashtami and Navami tithis. Commemorates Goddess Durga taking her fierce Chamunda form to kill demons Chanda and Munda.
Maha Aarti: Grand lamp-waving with conch shells, bells, and dhak drums

purpose.description: Dasami is the final day of Durga Puja and marks the immersion of Goddess Durga's idol in water.
purpose.addtional_description:
Durga Visarjan on Vijaya Dashami is the emotional farewell ceremony marking the end of Durga Puja celebrations. This ritual involves the ceremonial immersion of clay idols of Goddess Durga in rivers or water bodies, symbolizing her return to her celestial abode after her nine-day stay on Earth. 
Sindoor Utsav is a famous event during Durga Puja especially in West Bengal. On the day of Bengal Vijayadashami idols of Durga are immersed which culminates Durga Puja festivities. In the evening married women applies vermillion, famously known as Sindoor, to each other. After that Bijoya greetings and sweets are exchanged.

steps: Darpan Bisarjan: Final symbolic ceremony where Goddess's reflection is shown in mirror or water vessel. Represents taking leave of the Goddess before physical immersion
Sindur Khela (Vermilion Play): Married women first offer sindoor to Goddess Durga. Then apply vermilion to each other's faces and hair-partings
Bisarjan (Immersion) Process: Clay idols carried in grand procession with traditional drumming (dhak). Procession includes conch shells, cymbals, and devotional chants.

purpose.description: Vijayadashami is celebrated as victory of Lord Rama over Demon Ravana. Vijayadashami is also known as Dussehra or Dasara
purpose.addtional_description:
Vijayadashami is the tenth and final day of Sharad Navratri. The festival derives its name from 'Vijay' (victory) and 'Dashami' (tenth), meaning 'the day of victory'.

**Dual Significance:**
**Lord Rama's Victory:** Commemorates Rama's triumph over the ten-headed demon king Ravana, who had abducted Rama's wife Sita, as described in the Ramayana epic.
**Goddess Durga's Victory:** In eastern and southern India, marks Durga's slaying of the buffalo demon Mahishasura after nine days of battle

steps: Ramlila Performances: Dramatic enactments of Ramayana story over 9 days, culminating with Ravana's defeat.
Ravana Dahan: Burning of giant effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna, and Meghnad symbolizing destruction of evil.
Aparajita Puja: Worship of invincible goddess for victory and success
South India - Knowledge and Tools Worship:
Ayudha Puja: Worship of tools, instruments, books, and vehicles - honoring divine in implements of work
Vidyarambham/Aksharabhyasam: Initiation of children into education - writing "Om" on rice
Shami Puja: Worship of Shami (Jammi) tree, recalling Pandavas retrieving hidden weapons
Jammi Leaf Exchange: Exchanging Shami leaves as "gold" custom
Durga Visarjan: Grand procession carrying clay idols to river for immersion
Sindoor Khela: Married women smear vermilion while bidding farewell to Goddess Durga
Bishorjon: Immersion ceremony marking end of Durga Puja

purpose.description: Kojagari Puja is one of the major festivals celebrated in West Bengal, Odisha and Assam. A special worship of Goddess Lakshmi is performed on this day
purpose.addtional_description:
Meaning of "Kojagara": The term comes from the Sanskrit phrase "Ko Jagarti?" meaning "Who is awake?" - reflecting the core belief that Goddess Lakshmi visits Earth on this night and asks "Who is awake?" blessing only those who remain vigilant in devotion. 

According to the Kojagara Vrat Story, Goddess Lakshmi visits the world on the night of Ashwin Purnima and She bestows wealth and prosperity on those devotees who are awakened on this night.

Bhishma bowed for celibacy and followed it throughout his life. Due to his loyalty and devotion to his father Pitamah Bhishma was blessed with boon to choose the time of his death. When he got injured in the battle of Mahabharata he didn't leave his body due to his boon. He waited for the auspicious moment to give up his body

purpose.description: Auspicious fasting day dedicated to Lord Vishnu
purpose.addtional_description:
Ekadashi is the eleventh lunar day observed twice monthly (on Shukla Paksha and Krishna Paksha) dedicated to Lord Vishnu, considered one of the most meritorious fasts in Sanatana Dharma that purifies the mind, body, and soul while helping devotees gain control over their senses and overcome past sins.

The core rituals remain identical for both Shukla and Krishna Paksha Ekadashi, with the primary difference being that Shukla Paksha Ekadashi symbolizes growth and spiritual expansion, while Krishna Paksha Ekadashi focuses on introspection, renunciation, and inner purification.

steps: Sankalp (Vow Taking) Take a formal vow before Lord Vishnu by holding water in your right palm and stating your intention to observe the Ekadashi fast sincerely.
Morning Puja Worship Lord Vishnu with Tulsi leaves (most essential), yellow flowers, sandalwood paste, incense, and ghee lamps at the home altar.
Fasting Observance Observe the chosen fast type - Nirjala (no food/water), Phalahar (fruits/milk only), or Farali (sattvic foods) while completely avoiding grains, rice, pulses, onion, and garlic.
Katha Reading Listen to or recite the specific Ekadashi story associated with that particular tithi, as reading the katha is considered as important as the fast itself.

Parana (Breaking Fast) Break the fast on Dwadashi morning after sunrise by first offering food to Lord Vishnu, then feeding Brahmins or the needy, and finally consuming simple satvik food within the prescribed time window.
